items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
50% Facilitates and manages the administration of non-senate appointments. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Provide guidance on senate and non-senate academic personnel policies and procedures to the department leadership including the Department Chair, Vice Chairs, and Director of Administration.

Interpret and administer applicable academic personnel policies and labor contracts specific to non-senate job titles (pre-six lecturers, continuing lecturers, academic coordinators, specialists, project scientists, researchers, visitors, and postdocs), ensure that departmental practices and policies are in compliance, and request exceptions to policy where appropriate.

Conduct searches for applicable titles, supporting the search committee and administering the search through the campus recruitment system (currently AP Recruit), guide search committees on equitable hiring practices, draft search plans/reports, manage applicant materials, and coordinate candidate interviews. etc.

Oversee administration of academic appointments in campus applicable campus human resource management and payroll systems (currently UCPath), ensuring data accuracy, timely compensation processing, retroactive payments, and correcting errors when necessary.
Manage the merit and review process for departmental non-senate appointments including excellence reviews for pre-six lecturers, promotion to Sr. lecturers and continuing lecturers’ merits.
Assess and summarize data and comments from teaching evaluations and maintain information related to case reviews including, semesters of teaching, and convert and prepare data for case presentation.
Coordinate appointment terminations for appropriate titles, including temporary or permanent augmentations and layoffs.
Act as a liaison between the department and ERSO team for non-senate and senate academic activities.
Oversee communications with senate and non-senate appointments including administration of appropriate distribution lists and preparing communications and documents for distribution.
Provide applicable reporting on non-senate titles and activities.
20% Provide back-up and support to the Academic HR Analyst in charge of senate academic appointments (faculty, LSOE’s, Emeritus, Professors of the Graduate School, etc.):
Assist in the full-cycle of all academic cases and pending academic personnel activities for a small number of ladder-rank senate faculty, and instructors.
Prepare materials for academic review cases within defined allocation and correspond directly with candidates to solicit and prepare required materials.
Work with senate faculty within assigned allocation to enter data into AP cases and upload to APBears.
Coordinate with assigned senate faculty throughout merit, promotion, and appointment case review.
Manage faculty leave records for all senate faculty appointments and administer academic leaves and sabbaticals.
Act as a liaison between the department, college, and campus Academic Personnel offices for assigned Senate faculty matters.
Support Search Committee & Recruitment Administration:

Assist in the coordination of Senate search processes in AP Recruit; draft search plans, post advertisements, coordinate candidate itineraries, attend committee meetings, and advise search committees on equitable hiring practices.
Coordinate appointment requests with the Dean’s Office for titles not supported by Berkeley Regional Services.
Submit and monitor HR and payroll transactions for faculty and other academic appointments, including lecturers, ensuring accurate and timely processing.
Attend faculty meetings as requested, prepare necessary meeting materials, and oversee the administration of faculty ballots.
15% Administrative operations for a large academic department:
Coordinate the use of departmental resources, such as shared space and facilities, and manage equipment needs; update departmental and university calendars.

Ensure the daily administrative operations run smoothly for the department, which include complex travel arrangements, travel & entertainment reimbursement processing, and resource management while maintaining common areas. Troubleshoot and resolve issues as needed.
Supervisor - schedule hours of work and vacation schedules for student reception team, including hiring, providing direction, performance feedback, correctional actions, firing, and mentoring.
Determine staffing needs then coordinate and activate staff, delegate tasks, and coordinate with managers and program team for events not handled by event coordinator.
15% Executive support to the Department Chair. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Independently evaluate, screen, and prioritize (and when appropriate redirect) requests to the Chair's Office from faculty, other administrators, and outside agencies.
Apply discretion and knowledge of set priorities to manage information flow.
Independently assess and respond to correspondence on behalf of the Chair, and prepare comprehensive written communications on the Chair's behalf.
Prioritize and manage the Chair's to-do list, provide timely briefings, advise on priorities and deadlines, and track status of pending issues.
Manage the Chair's calendar and support prioritization of appointments, deadlines, and initiatives.
Draft communications on behalf of the Chair.
In conjunction with the Director of Administration, provide continuity and aid in the smooth transition from one Chair to the next.
Excellent critical and innovative thinking to address complex issues and present nuanced analyses.
Attention to detail, discretion and sensitivity to confidential information.
Developed political acumen.
In-depth knowledge of and ability to apply/interpret campus and college policies and procedures which govern academic HR in an academic setting, preferably within the UC System.
Thorough knowledge of academic based policies, union contracts, procedures and practices that govern academic HR administration.
Thorough knowledge of campus and college goals, priorities and values and the legal and human implications of decisions.
Ability to analyze complex management issues; develop project scope and solutions, give professional advice to senior officials and make critical decisions regarding personnel.
Excellent verbal and written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Strong computer skills including work processing, spreadsheets and data base management.
Ability to identify and resolve problems of moderate complexity.
